We need to determine if we can reduce an array to zero by repeatedly subtracting 1 from any subarray of length k. Equivalent to: can we apply operations of decrementing a sliding window of size k to achieve zero? This is similar to problem "Check if Array Is Good" or "Minimum Number of K Consecutive Bit Flips" but for decrements.

Observations: Operation reduces each element in a subarray by exactly 1 per operation. Since we can apply many times, we can think of representing each operation as adding a certain amount (negative) to a range. We need to find non-negative integer x_i for each position i (starting index of subarray) such that for each position j, sum_{i: i <= j < i+k} x_i = nums[j] (the total decrements applied to position j). This is like solving a system of linear equations with sliding window length k. Equivalent to performing a greedy left-to-right algorithm: at each index i, we maintain the cumulative effect of previous operations that affect i. If after considering previous operations, the current value at i (nums[i] minus effect) is negative, impossible; if positive, we need to start operations at i to reduce it to zero; each operation at i will affect positions i..i+k-1, so we add its effect to a sliding window sum and maybe push to a queue; after moving beyond i+k-1 we remove its effect.

Thus algorithm: Use difference array or sliding window sum variable cur representing total decrements applied to current index from operations started in the previous k-1 positions. Iterate i from 0 to n-1:

- cur holds total decrements applied to nums[i] from earlier operations (those started at indices i-k+1 ... i-1) - actually from operations whose windows cover i.

- effective = nums[i] - cur. If effective < 0: return False (we have over-decremented).

- If effective > 0: we need to start effective new operations at index i (each subtract 1 from subarray i..i+k-1). So we add effective to cur (since these operations affect current index). Also we need to remember to subtract their effect after they expire: we can push effective onto a queue (or array) to be subtracted when we move out of range.
